answer: Check the idle clock. Each identity holds a reputation score that decays every epoch without a submission, and every unverified claim shaves it again. Submit a job, get it attested, reset the clock. Skip one epoch and the score drops; skip six and the identity falls under the grading threshold. Treat the score as water in an inlet: it stays full only while work flows, and a whisper of idle time reaches the jury before the payout does. A farmer holding a thousand aliases must feed all of them every epoch, and the basalt floor is where the cheapest attack costs more than the work it imitates.
